title: Visual field progression in glaucoma: what is the specificity of the Guided Progression Analysis?
what_they_did: Estimated GPA 'possible'/'likely progression' false-positive rate in 30 glaucoma eyes tested 12 times over 3 months, re-analysing 1000 random re-orderings of each retest series; FP varied <1% to 80% between patients
c (dataset; context): 30 OAG patients, 12 weekly-ish SITA-Std 24-2 tests (the same retest data we use as E2)
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: They measured true-null specificity of one event method (GPA) only; we measure it for 10 detectors including supervised ML and conformal methods at k=3-6, and test whether shuffling CLINIC series predicts that true-null rate.

title: Hierarchical Censored Bayesian Analysis of Visual Field Progression
what_they_did: Hierarchical Bayesian VF progression models vs OLS and PoPLR compared at matched false-positive rate, FPR quantified by permutations of a separate test-retest cohort
c (dataset; context): 44,371 VFs/3,352 eyes from 5 clinics; FPR from 360 tests of 30 glaucoma eyes (identity with Artes data UNVERIFIED)
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: They used permuted retest data to equalise FPR of a few model-based methods; we report the raw (un-equalised) true-null FAR of each detector as calibrated in practice, include supervised ML, and validate a clinic-shuffle audit against the true null.

title: Detection of Longitudinal Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma Using Machine Learning
what_they_did: ML (pattern-based) progression index vs global MD, region-wise and pointwise criteria; all thresholds set to 95% specificity on a no-change test-retest set (133 eyes, 10 tests over 10 weeks); survival comparison in independent cohort
c (dataset; context): 2,085 eyes (training patterns); 133 retest eyes; 270 longitudinal eyes
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: They calibrated the ML index ON true no-change data (so its FAR is controlled by construction); we show what happens when supervised ML is calibrated on clinic 'reference-stable' labels (FAR 19-28% on true null) and evaluate only at 3-6 tests.

title: Combining optical coherence tomography with visual field data to rapidly detect disease progression in glaucoma: a diagnostic accuracy study
what_they_did: HTA comparison of GPA, PoPLR, ANSWERS, sANSWERS and new methods (PERM, MaHMIC, MaGIC); specificity set at 95% using RAPID stable glaucoma patients with 11 VF+OCT tests within 3 months; hit rates in UKGTS
c (dataset; context): UKGTS + RAPID (72 stable patients, 11 tests in 3 months)
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: Same design idea (true short-term no-change cohort for specificity, multi-method comparison) but no supervised ML, no shuffle-vs-true-null validation, not restricted to 3-6 tests, data not open.

title: Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma: Comparison Between PoPLR and ANSWERS
what_they_did: PoPLR vs ANSWERS in three cohorts; FP rate estimated by randomly re-ordering series in time; ANSWERS FP 15-17% at nominal 5% vs PoPLR 3-7%; positive rates compared after equating specificity
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: Closest precedent for 'sophisticated method has inflated FAR'; but they use re-ordered clinic series only (no true-null retest arm), study a parametric model not supervised ML, and do not test whether the shuffle estimate matches a true null.

title: Visual field progression in glaucoma: estimating the overall significance of deterioration with permutation analyses of pointwise linear regression (PoPLR)
what_they_did: Introduced PoPLR (within-eye permutation of the series); FP rates estimated from randomly reordered series of the cohort; PoPLR FP matched nominal levels; compared to PLR at matched specificity
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: Established permutation both as a test and as a specificity estimator; we use PoPLR as one detector and ask how well the shuffle estimate agrees with true no-change FAR across 10 detectors at k=3-6.

title: Detection of Functional Change Using Cluster Trend Analysis in Glaucoma
what_they_did: Cluster trend analysis; criteria set to exactly 95% specificity from re-orderings of 133 test-retest eyes (7-10 tests); global vs pointwise vs cluster compared on 505 long series
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: Uses permuted true-retest data to calibrate classical criteria; no ML, long series, no comparison of clinic-shuffle vs true-null FAR.

title: Detecting Change Using Standard Global Perimetric Indices in Glaucoma
what_they_did: MD vs VFI vs PSD trend; critical P set so 5% of test-retest series (5 tests, random order artificial dates) show deterioration; time-to-detect compared
c (dataset; context): 45 test-retest eyes (5 tests short interval); 508 longitudinal eyes
one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: Same 'calibrate on permuted true retest series' logic for global indices at a 5-test horizon; no ML/conformal methods, no shuffle-audit validation.

one_precise_sentence_how_ours_differs: OCT not VF; uses scrambling as a training signal (analogue of our self-supervised order network) and equalises specificity, but no true no-change arm and no audit of whether scrambled-sequence FAR equals true-null FAR.

title: Comparing the Rule of 5 to Trend-based Analysis for Detecting Glaucoma Progression on OCT
